title: How Walk Me Through works
summary: A coding agent authors the journey. Python validates and snapshots the code. Your browser turns that document into a step-through explanation. Follow the full path or inspect a rejected build.

steps.title: 1. Turn the question into one concrete journey
steps.explanation: The coding agent chooses one user action, follows its actual callers and callees in current source, and identifies boundaries such as HTTP requests and background threads. This is agent reasoning guided by the skill, not executable analysis code. No knowledge graph or external analysis plugin is involved.

inputs.request: Show how a review sync reaches persisted alignment state

outputs.scope: One review-sync journey, including a relevant failure path

steps.title: 2. The agent writes the explanation as JSON
steps.explanation: The agent authors step descriptions, source ranges, illustrative inputs/outputs/state, and explicit scenario paths. The builder does not infer the workflow or invent explanations: it consumes this document. The code excerpt is the skill’s schema example, not a real source path in this plugin.

state.explanation: Written by the agent; example values are illustrative

steps.title: 3. Run the deterministic builder
steps.explanation: The command-line entry point accepts the project root, authored flow JSON, and HTML output path, then calls build(). No model or remote API is invoked by this Python program.

steps.title: 4. Load JSON and validate step structure
steps.explanation: build() resolves the root and parses the workflow JSON. It requires a title, summary, steps, scenarios, unique step IDs, explanations, boundary descriptions, and object-shaped example data. These checks prevent broken data from reaching the viewer; they do not prove the narrative is semantically correct.

steps.title: 5. Resolve the source path inside the project
steps.explanation: For every step, the builder resolves the referenced path and rejects absolute paths or paths outside the project root. Resolving symlinks before checking containment also prevents a link inside the project from pointing to an outside file. It then reads the referenced text.

steps.title: 6. Embed the exact source range
steps.explanation: The builder validates line ranges, embeds those exact source lines, and hashes the full raw source bytes. The displayed code remains a snapshot. Optional folder access lets the viewer later compare hashes against live files without replacing the embedded code or rewriting the explanation.

outputs.source.sha256: SHA256 of the full raw source bytes

steps.title: 7. Validate scenario paths
steps.explanation: Each scenario is an explicit ordered list of step IDs. The builder rejects duplicate scenario IDs, missing titles/descriptions/paths, and references to unknown steps. It does not infer branches or prove that a listed sequence executes at runtime.

steps.title: 8. Package data and source into one HTML file
steps.explanation: The builder records Git HEAD and build time, loads the viewer template, embeds the freshness-check script, and inserts the enriched workflow JSON. Escaping < prevents source text from closing the JSON script element. It writes one standalone HTML file.

steps.title: 9. Browser loads the embedded workflow
steps.explanation: This starts a new phase: the user opens the generated HTML in a browser. JavaScript parses the embedded JSON, indexes steps by ID, selects the first scenario and starts at index zero. It populates the scenario selector. There is no server request or application execution.

outputs.byId: Map from step IDs to step objects

steps.title: 10. Render the selected step and its code
steps.explanation: render() chooses the step at the current scenario index, draws the flow buttons, and fills the explanation, exact numbered source lines, and example data panels. Text is inserted with textContent or text nodes rather than interpreted as HTML. It also updates progress, button bounds, and source provenance.
steps.boundary: Browser state → flowchart and detail panels

outputs.screen: Submit step highlighted, its code and example state visible

state.application state: Unaffected; displayed state is explanatory example data

steps.title: 11. Change scenario, navigate, or inspect state
steps.explanation: Changing scenarios pauses playback and resets the index. Back/Next change the index and call render(). Tabs toggle visibility of code and example-state panels. Clicking a flow step likewise changes the selected index (shown in render()). The data is already embedded in the page.

inputs.action: Choose a scenario, click Next, or open Example data & state

outputs.screen: Updated selected step or detail tab

steps.title: 12. Playback advances explanations, not application code
steps.explanation: Play starts an interval that increments the index every 3.5 seconds and rerenders. At the last step it pauses; Play from the end restarts. Page hiding also pauses playback. Nothing calls your API, runs the displayed Python, or evaluates the example state.

outputs.screen: Next step highlighted with its code and examples

state.timer: Active until paused, hidden, or finished

steps.title: Build stops: the source escapes the project
steps.explanation: The source-containment guard raises ValueError. The caller has no catch that turns this into a partial viewer, so the build exits before output.write_text(). If a prior HTML exists, it remains the old artifact; a failed build does not refresh it.

outputs.exception: ValueError: Source must be inside the project

steps.title: Build stops: a source range is no longer valid
steps.explanation: If the requested range no longer fits the file, validation raises ValueError before saving. This catches out-of-bounds references; a range that still fits but now points to different logic requires the agent to review and update the narrative.

steps.title: Build stops: a scenario names a missing step
steps.explanation: The document can have valid code snippets but still be unusable if a path points to a nonexistent step. This guard rejects that path before an HTML file is saved. The agent should correct the JSON and rebuild.

outputs.exception: ValueError: Scenario references an unknown step

steps.title: Select the project source folder
steps.explanation: Check source folder uses the live browser folder API when available. If the API is unavailable or blocked, a standard folder input performs a one-time comparison. No selected files are uploaded. Live handles last for this page session; one-time selections must be repeated after editing.

steps.title: Compare current bytes with snapshot hashes
steps.explanation: The checker reads each referenced file from either the live folder handle or a one-time folder selection, and hashes its raw bytes with the browser crypto API. Changed, missing, and unreadable files are tracked separately. Both access modes use the same comparison.

state.filesystem: Read-only; source snippets stay embedded snapshots

steps.title: Show match, stale, or unverified status
steps.explanation: Changed or missing files mark the HTML Out of date; access failures remain unverified. Matching files verify only referenced sources. Live access supports manual, focus, and 30-second rechecks. With the standard picker, select the folder again after edits to perform a new comparison; the page does not reuse old file snapshots as if they were live.

outputs.banner: Out of date — referenced sources differ

state.freshness: match → stale; can return to match after restoration

scenarios.title: Request → generated HTML → playback
scenarios.description: The full reconstructed workflow. The first two steps are agent instructions, the middle steps run in Python, and the final steps run in your browser after you open the output.

scenarios.title: Rejected build · source outside project
scenarios.description: An authored step references ../private.txt. Follow the guard that stops the build before an HTML file is written.

scenarios.title: Rejected build · source range drifted
scenarios.description: The file now has only 80 lines, but the authored reference requests lines 90–110. The builder rejects this range.

scenarios.title: Rejected build · unknown step in scenario
scenarios.description: Source snapshots can be valid while the scenario references a nonexistent step. Path validation catches this before saving.

scenarios.title: Test freshness · change a referenced file
scenarios.description: Select the plugin folder, check the hashes, then append a blank line to SKILL.md and click Recheck now. Undo the blank line to return to matching sources. These are illustrative steps; you control the actual edit.
